newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZI Life up for sale - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: NZI Life up for sale - newspaper.

text.p: New Zealand's third-biggest life insurer, NZI Life, is up for sale but parent company General Accident will hold on to its NZI fire and general business in New Zealand, the Dominion newspaper reported on Thursday.
Sir Ron Brierley's Guinness Peat Group, AMP Society and Prudential have all been touted as potential buyers but all three declined to comment.
A sale is expected to be completed by the end of March, the Dominion said.

"The decision to hold discussions with potential buyers of NZI Life is based on General Accident's global strategy to concentrate on building its fire and general insurance business in markets where it has a significant presence and is market leader," the paper quoted communications manager Callum Spreng, from General Accident's head office in Scotland, as saying.
General Accident's life insurance activities will be concentrated in its British market, where life insurance is part of the company's core business.
"In New Zealand, where we are the market leader in fire and general insurance, this means focusing on that core business through New Zealand Insurance."

NZI Life had been attracting interest from buyers for some time. NZI Life has about NZ$1.3 billion in assets under management, 350 staff and 220 agents. Annual premium income is about NZ$175 million, with about 310,000 policies in force.
It is the third-biggest life insurance company out of 26 in New Zealand, with a market share of 9.1 percent.
GPG's subsidiary Tyndall Australia bought New Zealand Guardian Trust Co, which manages investments for NZI Life, from General Accident in 1994 for NZ$20 million.
